conventions.convention: All real variables, limits, derivatives and integrals are interpreted in a Dedekind-complete ordered field.
Continuity on a closed interval is relative continuity; derivatives at interior points are two-sided difference-quotient limits. C^(n+1) is defined on an open interval.

The dyadic format has precision p ≥ 2, bounded integer exponents, signed subnormals of quantum 2^(emin-p+1), and infinite enclosure sentinels. Directed rounding brackets exact values; epsilon_abs(0)=0 and overflow has infinite error bound.
Finite real intervals have finite dyadic endpoints. Computation statuses are not finite intervals. Rectangle width is Euclidean diameter and ball width is twice its radius.

Division through zero returns a non-finite status. Complex-rectangle reciprocal denominators remain exact until final component rounding. Ball operations use conservative origin-centered output balls.
Riemann integrals are oriented: the integral from a point to itself is zero, and reversing endpoints negates the integral.
Pi is 4 arctan(1), where arctangent is the integral of 1/(1+t²). Principal complex Log excludes the entire nonpositive real axis, including zero.
Nesting comparisons keep the DAG, constant enclosures, format and truncation index fixed. Canonical branch cells and the same Machin interval are reused throughout each call.
The split budget is shared across the entire queue. A split midpoint must belong to the selected format; certification requires a final width test on the hull of all completed leaves.

load_bearing.statement: For defined operations on real intervals, complex rectangles or complex balls, enlarging inputs preserves inclusion whenever both results are finite and domain restrictions are preserved. Square-root enclosure is inclusion-isotone on nonnegative intervals. For a finite expression DAG whose operation nodes all return finite enclosures, every exact node value from every admissible input assignment belongs to its computed node enclosure. A non-finite status asserts no finite DAG enclosure.

For finite x with |x| ≤ Nmax, rd(x) ≤ x ≤ ru(x), and each endpoint error is at most the stated epsilon_abs(x), with zero error for representable x. Beyond the finite range, the prescribed finite/infinite endpoint pairs enclose x; overflow has infinite error bound.

The power-series sine and cosine satisfy their addition identities and sin²x+cos²x=1. With pi=4 arctan(1), pi=16 arctan(1/5)-4 arctan(1/239). Every real input has a quarter-period reduction with residual magnitude at most pi/4. On residuals of magnitude at most 1, the displayed geometric bounds enclose the omitted sine and cosine tails.

Every finite interval returned for a requested real elementary output contains the exact range on its input interval. For the same typed DAG, designated real output, fixed constant enclosures, format and truncation index, coordinatewise nested inputs give nested computed enclosures whenever both calls return finite results.

Every finite complex exponential or principal-logarithm output contains the exact image on its admissible rectangle. Nested inputs on the same admissible branch give nested finite enclosures for the same typed DAG, fixed constants, format and truncation index.

For every finite input DAG and finite total split budget B, the budgeted algorithm terminates. If it returns certified(I,X), then I contains the exact function range on all of X and has width at most the requested epsilon. Other statuses make no unconditional tolerance-success claim.

For n ≥ 0 and f with continuous derivatives through order n+1 on an open interval containing the segment between c and x, f(x)-Pn(x) equals the displayed oriented integral remainder. If |f^(n+1)| ≤ M on that segment, its absolute value is at most M|x-c|^(n+1)/(n+1)!, including x=c.

concerns.concern: The Statement asserts unconditionally, 'Under the hypotheses in [[def-centered-taylor-model-with-derivative-interval]], f(X) ⊆ T_n(...)'. Those hypotheses do not require a finite arithmetic result, although the model is evaluated using operations that return overflow statuses, which def-intervals-rectangles-and-complex-balls explicitly distinguishes from finite intervals. Concrete admissible data: p=2, emin=0, emax=2 give Nmax=6; take f(t)=6t, X=[0,2], c=0, n=1, C0=[0,0], C1=[6,6], D=[0,0]. All supplied endpoints are representable and all analytic hypotheses hold, but the polynomial product has exact upper endpoint 12 and returns overflow. Thus the asserted set inclusion has no defined finite model enclosure in this case. Proof 2.1 applies the finite-result DAG theorem without establishing its finite-result hypothesis.

The Statement includes uniform absolute convergence of the geometric series 'with their formal derivative series' on |x| ≤ r < 1. Proof 1.1 handles the geometric series itself, while Proof 4.1 handles the odd series and its derivative; neither establishes convergence of the geometric derivative majorant Σ n r^(n-1). An eventual-ratio geometric bound closes this short omitted argument.

seams_checked.note: The owned page explicitly retains this requirement as reading context and consumes no factorization, solve-bound or round-to-nearest success premise. Its local directed-rounding construction does not strengthen the factorization page's conditional arithmetic contracts.

alg-box-muller-finite-bit-transform uses certified log/root intervals, derives endpoint error bounds from their widths, and propagates failed supplier calls as inconclusive. It does not infer unconditional evaluator success or a distribution law from conditional arithmetic certification.

The residual-tube definition, checker and soundness proof use finite real rational-DAG enclosures after outward conversion of rational inputs. Non-finite operations prevent certification; no unsupported transcendental or ball evaluator is attributed to the supplier.

The phase routine constructs a Machin enclosure, evaluates sine/cosine with fixed finite parameters, and certifies only after checking an outward coordinate-width bound. The separate pi bridge identifies the interval convention with the Fourier convention. Precision-cap failures remain inconclusive.

Certified Simpson uses finite outward arithmetic and upward rounding of a separately proved remainder allowance. Valid point and derivative oracles are explicit caller hypotheses, midpoint representability is checked, and non-finite operations return failure.

The interval determinant, LDL, Krawczyk, residual, spectral and resolvent validators use finite arithmetic-DAG enclosure only. Their success proofs apply it to admitted finite runs; unresolved divisions, signs and range bounds do not establish singularity or certification.

The local arithmetic lemma faithfully reproduces finite-result enclosure and failure qualifications. Scalar Newton requires a derivative interval excluding zero; the Jacobian mean-value proof uses the scalar MVT separately for each row and explicitly avoids claiming a common intermediate Jacobian.

The DAG bound routine outward-converts arbitrary real input endpoints before interval operations and propagates non-finite statuses. Its consistency theorem additionally requires increasing precision, convergent constant enclosures, protected division denominators and an exponent range avoiding overflow; these are not inferred from finite-precision soundness alone.
